name: Indecency with a child (sexual contact)
conduct: Engaging in sexual contact with the child or causing the child to engage in sexual contact. Section 21.11(c) requires intent to arouse or gratify anyone’s sexual desire and covers the listed touching, including through clothing, of a child’s anus, breast or genitals, or touching any part of the child’s body with another person’s anus, breast or genitals. Incidental touching without the statutory sexual intent is not silently included. The child must be younger than 17, regardless of knowledge of age. Subsection (b) states a close-in-age affirmative defense requiring no more than a three-year age gap, its opposite-sex condition, no duress/force/threat, and the stated registration-status alternative; its application to a particular case must be evaluated rather than assumed from age alone. Subsection (b-1) separately supplies a spouse affirmative defense.
penalty: Second-degree felony: ordinarily two to 20 years in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. These are ordinary ranges, not a determination that no special prior applies. Section 12.42 can require life or life without parole for specified repeat sexual offenses; the exact current offense, prior, age and other statutory findings require separate review. Conviction for this offense is reportable under Chapter 62 and carries registration consequences; duration, reporting duties and any statutory relief depend on the exact record. For qualifying multiple convictions from one criminal episode, §3.03 permits consecutive sentences rather than guaranteeing concurrent service.

name: Sexual assault (child: penetration of anus or sexual organ)
conduct: Intentionally or knowingly causes penetration of the child’s anus or sexual organ by any means. Child means younger than 17. Knowledge of the child’s age is not required. The §22.011(d) medical-care defense is limited to care without the prohibited child-to-actor/third-party sexual contact. The spouse and close-in-age affirmative defenses in §22.011(e) have their own conditions: the latter requires no more than a three-year age gap, a victim at least 14, the statutory registration-status alternative, and no prohibited §25.01/§25.02 relationship. It is not a blanket consent or age-gap exception. Section 22.011(f)(1) raises the grade for the specified prohibited marriage/intercourse relationships; the ordinary range does not erase that branch. Conduct against a child younger than 14 may also meet the separate aggravated offense; this choice does not promise nonaggravated treatment.
penalty: Second-degree felony: ordinarily two to 20 years in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. The §22.011(f)(1) prohibited-relationship branch is first degree: ordinarily five to 99 years or life and up to $10,000. These are ordinary ranges, not a determination that no special prior applies. Section 12.42 can require life or life without parole for specified repeat sexual offenses; the exact current offense, prior, age and other statutory findings require separate review. name: Sexual Assault
conduct: The statute covers intentional or knowing penetration/contact under (a)(1) without consent under the specific (b) circumstances, or the separately enumerated child conduct under (a)(2). The child alternatives are penetration of anus/sexual organ by any means, mouth penetration by the actor’s sexual organ, child sexual-organ contact with another’s mouth/anus/sexual organ, child anus contact with those parts, or child mouth contact with another’s anus/sexual organ. The spouse and close-in-age affirmative defenses in §22.011(e) have their own conditions: the latter requires no more than a three-year age gap, a victim at least 14, the statutory registration-status alternative, and no prohibited §25.01/§25.02 relationship. It is not a blanket consent or age-gap exception. The nonconsent alternatives include specified compulsion, incapacity or unawareness and enumerated exploitation/relationship circumstances; this whole-statute identity does not determine which one a case proves. The prohibited-relationship first-degree and assisted-reproduction state-jail branches remain distinct.
